items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: we got to meet everybody who came through The Sands. Now that’s Sinatra, Nat King Cole, Jerry Lewis, on and on and on.

ctx.x: And it was really nice living there too, because even though it was Las Vegas, it wasn’t like it is now, it was just like a little sleepy town except for the Strip. The Strip had all the big casinos and everything, and that was kind of bright and wonderful and a lot of great people were coming into the showroom, and so eventually we worked the Thunderbird, and we just started working the gambling circuit because we could have the kids in school, we could be there all the time, and it was another answer to our…

In the summer we would take them on the road with us again. We’d go to Reno, go to Lake Tahoe, then make a swing through San Francisco and go down to L.A. and back to Las Vegas, and this time go into The Sands for a year, opposite the Red Norvo Quintet. And that was wonderful, because here we had a good group, a tight group, and Red had a © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
fantastic group. So we were there for a year and we got to meet everybody who came through The Sands. Now that’s Sinatra, Nat King Cole, Jerry Lewis, on and on and on.
